one_liner: Header-only C++17 sparse, unbounded VDB-style voxel grid; first-party preliminary numbers show 4.5-22x faster inserts and iteration than Octomap.
what_it_does: Bonxai stores arbitrary per-voxel values (int, float, Eigen vectors, user structs) on an unbounded 3D grid with 32-bit integer coordinates, allocating memory only where cells exist. The core API is VoxelGrid<T>(voxel_size) plus Accessor objects (setValue, value, forEachCell, posToCoord/coordToPos); it is not Octomap-API-compatible. An optional bonxai_map layer adds ProbabilisticMap, an Octomap-style log-odds occupancy map with ray casting (insertPointCloud), and bonxai_ros wraps it for ROS 2.
how_it_is_fast: It implements a shallow OpenVDB-style hierarchy (Museth, 'VDB', ACM TOG 2013): a root hash map from block key to an inner grid (default 4^3 bitmask-indexed slots) whose slots point to dense leaf grids (default 8^3 values plus an occupancy bitmask), so a lookup is one hash probe and two array indexes instead of an octree descent. The root map is a custom CoordMap (open addressing, linear probing over 16-byte buckets, values that never move), Accessors cache the last root/inner/leaf so spatially coherent writes skip the hash, leaf blocks for trivial types come from a pooled block allocator, and iteration walks set bits in the masks.
when_to_use: Robotics or 3D-mapping code that inserts many points per scan into a sparse voxel map and finds Octomap's per-point insertion too slow.
Storing custom per-voxel payloads (TSDF values, colours, counters, small structs) without a fixed map boundary.
Spatially coherent access patterns (scan lines, neighbouring voxels) where the accessor cache avoids most root-map lookups.
Fast full-map traversal (forEachCell) for publishing or exporting the map.
Projects that want a small vendorable core: the README says the core data structure is under 1,000 lines and header-only.
when_not_to_use: Very sparse clouds where memory matters: the README says Bonxai can use 20-40% more memory than Octomap there.
You need multi-resolution queries, octree pruning or Octomap's file formats and ecosystem tools; Bonxai is a single-resolution grid.
Concurrent writers: VoxelGrid is not thread-safe for writes.

Safety-critical code without testing: the author calls it a project built 'mostly for fun and for educational purposes', still under development, and memory-safety bugs in accessors and the leaf pool were being fixed as recently as September 2026 (issue #71 open).
Decisions based on the published speedup: the README numbers are labelled preliminary, give no compiler, CPU or dataset, and compare a plain value store against Octomap's probabilistic update.

integration.form: header-only (bonxai_core, CMake INTERFACE target Bonxai::bonxai_core); bonxai_map and bonxai_ros are optional built components
integration.dependencies: none for the core; bonxai_map needs Eigen3 (and is only built when PCL is found); benchmarks need Google Benchmark, PCL and octomap (NanoVDB for its comparison); LZ4 optional; bonxai_ros needs ROS 2 (rclcpp, tf2, pcl_conversions)
integration.platforms: portable C++17 with no SIMD intrinsics in the core (GCC/Clang and MSVC attribute macros present); ROS 2 Humble/Jazzy support in bonxai_ros
integration.thread_safety: Not thread-safe for writes; read-only multithreading is allowed if each thread uses its own accessor (README). The leaf block allocator itself takes a mutex.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it replaces Octomap's OcTree for storing occupancy through bonxai_map::ProbabilisticMap (log-odds hit/miss, clamping, ray casting), but the API, map files and multi-resolution queries differ

gotchas: Erasing roots or clearing the map through rootMap() frees nodes that accessors may have cached; the header says to recreate accessors afterwards (issue #71 shows a heap-use-after-free reproduction for that pattern). clear() and releaseUnusedMemory() are handled by an epoch counter.
Moving a VoxelGrid broke its pooled leaves until the 2026-09-28 fix commit ('a moved VoxelGrid keeps its pooled leaves and invalidates accessors'); use a recent main.
Older code double-destroyed LeafGrid and double-freed Mask::words_ when leaf_bits >= 4 (fixed per an in-source comment), so non-default grid shapes are less battle-tested.
The default CMake build type is RelWithDebInfo, so set Release explicitly before benchmarking.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Bonxai when you need a sparse voxel map that stores values per cell (an Octomap or occupancy-grid replacement). ikd-Tree, nanoflann and PH-tree answer nearest-neighbour or range queries over points, and small_gicp's voxel grid only downsamples clouds for registration.
verified_claims_summary: The README's preliminary Google Benchmark block (bonxai_core/benchmark, PCD clouds table_scene_mug_rgb at 1 cm or room_scan at 5 cm; which one, and the compiler and CPU, are not stated) reports Create 1165 vs 25522 us, Update 851 vs 3824 us and IterateAllCells 124 vs 698 us against Octomap (about 21.9x, 4.5x and 5.6x, derived from page data). Per point, Bonxai only stores a uint32, while Octomap runs OcTree::updateNode, a probabilistic log-odds update. The like-for-like full-mapping harness (bonxai_map/benchmark/benchmark_kitti.cpp, ProbabilisticMap vs OcTree::insertPointCloud on KITTI) and a NanoVDB harness exist, but no results from them are published.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-09-28, 879 stars, 1 open and 24 closed issues), MPL-2.0 (file-level copyleft, so the header-only core can be vendored into proprietary code if changes to its files are shared).
